Puppet World

Step into Puppet World, a magical roaming experience where giant luminous puppets come to life, transforming Children's festival into a world of wonder and imagination. wering above the crowd, these illuminated characters gracefully dance, interact with visito and create unforgettable moments for audiences of all ages. Don't miss the chance of attending this parade with family and friends!

1, 2, 3, A Little Space for Me

Small spaces can hold big discoveries. Designed for children under three with their parents, this environment is divided into three distinct zones: movement, hands-on exploration, and quiet play. Each area offers a different way to engage, from active motion to focused interaction and calm building. The experience supports early development through movement, touch, and shared exploration.

1, 2, 3, Let's Rhyme!

Come sing along with us as we explore beloved nursery rhymes, discover new ones, and enjoy a wonderful storytelling experience. Connect with other families in a welcoming environment that promotes early childhood development and provides lots of entertainment. This session, lasting for 30 minutes, is ideal for children aged 0 to 3 years.

A Home I Imagine

A home can begin as an idea and take shape in many forms. In this workshop, imagination leads the design process. Through drawing, building, and assembling materials, children develop their own vision of a home and translate it into a tangible model. Each creation results in a constructed home that reflects personal ideas and vision.

Ajeeb in Wonder House

A story-led experience that follows Ajeeb as he visits a series of unusual homes, each shaped by a different idea, form, or function. As the story unfolds, children observe how each space reflects a way of living, then shift into designing a home that suits Ajeeb himself. The activity combines storytelling with creative decision-making, moving from observation to design.

Around the Table

An interactive activity where children explore how dining tables bring together different cultural practices. The program introduces a range of customs and habits from around the world, showing how the way people gather, sit, and share meals can differ from one place to another. Through simple role-play, children take part in everyday moments such as greeting others, welcoming guests, and spending time around a table.

Built by Nature

A bird&rsquo;s nest, a termite mound, a shell, each one is carefully built, not by chance, but by need. In this workshop, children observe how living things design their homes, then borrow these ideas to sketch and shape their own. Openings for air, layers for protection, and smart use of materials begin to appear in their designs. What starts in nature slowly turns into a built form.

Children's Café

Step into the Children&rsquo;s Caf&eacute;, a truly unique experience created just for your child! A space where little ones can enjoy their very own caf&eacute; moment, designed at their scale, where they choose, create and explore freely. From decorating their treats at the Art Toppings Station to relaxing in a cozy Reading Corner, every detail is made to spark joy and imagination. It&rsquo;s more than a caf&eacute;... it&rsquo;s a first-of-its-kind experience where children gain confidence in their creativity.

Drawing is one way to represent spaces, ideas, and everyday life to tell their stories through them. In this open drawing space, children use different materials to create images related to their home, activities, and surroundings.

Hidden Home Bingo

A simple object at home might have a story that starts far beyond the room it sits in. In this fast-paced bingo challenge, children move through clues and questions, connecting everyday items to the materials behind them. As matches come together, unexpected links appearو turning familiar spaces into something to decode and discover.

Insightful Spaces

The way we experience a space is shaped by what we feel under our feet, not just what we see. In this sensory journey, children touch different carpeted surfaces, noticing textures, patterns, and subtle changes in sensation. As they explore, they begin to recognize how materials influence comfort, sound and perception in everyday spaces.

Mic Moments

Everyday life is full of small details, routines, habits, and traditions that differ from one home to another. In this street mic&ndash;style activity, children respond to short, guided questions about their daily life. The format is open and conversational, allowing them to speak, listen, and hear different perspectives in a simple setup.

Mirror Or Window

Some images reflect what we already know, others reveal something new. In this interactive experience, artworks are explored as shifting viewpoints. Certain scenes echo familiar memories, while others introduce different ways of living and seeing the world. Through guided observation and creative response, children interpret what they see and translate it into visual expression. The experience results in personal interpretations shaped by both recognition and discovery.

My Family Bouquet

A bouquet grows, one flower at a time. In this hands-on workshop, children begin with simple shapes and watch them take form as each piece is rolled, combined, and built into a flower. Colors are chosen, details are added, and the process repeats, each new bloom adding to the whole. As the bouquet comes together, each flower stands for someone at home, gathered into one arrangement shaped through making and choice.

Our Place on Earth

A house in the desert is not built like one by the sea, and for good reason. In this experience, children explore how homes respond to their environments, from heat to movement to moisture. This leads into building and testing simple structures, adjusting them to stand against different conditions.

Treasures in Every Home

Deep within the Earth, metal begins its journey, formed over time and transformed into materials we use every day at home. In this interactive workshop, children follow this journey, then reshape a simple tin container into a new functional object. The activity introduces how materials can be reused and redesigned for new purposes..

Where We Belong

Look closely at Earth, and it begins to feel like a system that never stops working; air moving, water cycling, living things adapting. In this program, children explore how life continues and changes across different environments, and how organisms adjust to survive over time. The journey then stretches further, looking at how science studies these systems and reimagines them beyond Earth. The experience connects life, environment, and possibility in one continuous story.

Who Lived Here?

Every landscape shapes the homes built within it. This treasure hunt in Rehlaat Gallery, children follow clues across three environments: desert, mountain, and coast. Each stop reveals a model home designed in response to its surroundings, from materials and structure to layout and function. As they move between locations, children match clues to the correct homes, discovering how climate, terrain, and daily life influence the way people build and live.

Zoom In

A tiny fragment holds the clue. In this Praise of the Artisan treasure hunt, children begin with a zoomed-in detail taken from a larger artwork, a pattern, texture, or small visual hint. Moving through the space, they search for the full piece, matching what they see up close with what appears on the walls. As the search unfolds, attention shifts to details that are often overlooked, building observation skills through careful looking. Each match reveals the complete artwork behind the fragment.

In the Home of…

Some homes are easy to recognize. Others leave clues behind. In this interactive library experience, children move through a series of spaces, each one arranged as a &ldquo;home&rdquo; shaped by a well-known literary character. Objects, layouts, and small details hint at who might live there. As they explore each corner, children follow prompts and challenges that guide them to observe, connect, and identify the character behind each space. The experience unfolds step by step, turning the library into a trail of clues where stories are discovered through place, detail, and interaction.
